chunks: I said, 'A man married a woman. So when it was the night of the consummation, the woman brought a male friend of hers so she entered him into (one of) the rooms. So when the man entered in order to copulate with his wife, the friend leapt and they both fought in the house. So the husband killed the friend, and the woman stood up, so she struck the husband with a strike, so she killed him for the (killing of) the friend'.
So he said: 'The woman is responsible for the wergild of the friend, and she would be killed for (having killed her) husband'.

key_terms.تُقْتَلُ بِالزَّوْجِ: She is executed for the husband

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on blood money and execution when a wife kills her husband after he kills her friend during the wedding night?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'kaffarat al-dam' (blood expiation) where the wife assumes the financial liability (diyah) for the friend she introduced, while simultaneously facing execution (qisas) for the husband's life, highlighting the distinct legal categories of debt and retribution in Shia jurisprudence. Scholars note this case as a unique scenario where one party bears both the monetary compensation for a third party and the capital punishment for the primary victim, emphasizing the precision of hadith-based legal reasoning.
